scope: A real analysis started from Codex through the local IssueLens MCP server. It checks the integration (handshake, tool call, progress, timeout, report delivery), not analysis quality.
issue_choice: The web app's built-in example, already run live in M3, so this run isolates the Codex integration.

client.host_model: the user's default Codex model and reasoning effort (gpt-6-astra / max)
client.prompt: Use the issuelens MCP tool analyze_github_issue to analyze https://github.com/pallets/flask/issues/6146. Do not run shell commands or read local files. After the tool returns, reply with the report status, a two-sentence summary, the missing information, and the number of cited sources.
per_run_overrides: mcp_servers.issuelens: command through a logging relay, tool_timeout_sec = 180, default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"
node_repl, computer-use and pocket-notes disabled for this run
client.not_disabled: cua_repl, a JavaScript REPL provided by the Codex app, could not be disabled per run; overriding it made the configuration invalid. Codex did not call it.

server.settings: the checkout's .env, as for the web app

observations: Codex sent progressToken 1 on tools/call and accepted all progress notifications without an error, but codex exec --json emitted no progress events, so non-interactive Codex does not show progress. The interactive Codex UI was not checked.
The call took about 20 seconds, within Codex's 60-second default; the 180-second setting is still needed for runs near the 90-second budget.
Codex relayed the report's status, summary, missing information and source count faithfully and ran no commands.

The analysis was partial: the local context budget omitted one comment excerpt and forced early finalization. These are documented M2 limitations; the MCP server uses the same settings as the web app. The M3 live run of this issue was completed with 8 sources.
